_comment: World dressing P2-041 (OFF until GPU judged; coordinator Meshy Crown Arch, tb/props-r2 a2f81b50, assets/props/meshy-1031/crown_arch, provenance there). GPU 31 Oct 4.23 main / 4.56 octagonal landing; judges asked for a hero arch taller than the trainer with a crown keystone and crystal or copper accents, rooted in moss not on a slab. The Meshy arch replaces the visible arch at 5.5 m (3x the 1.80 m trainer); the old arch piece and slab mesh are hidden, not freed, so the 9x9 m footing collider, the 2.2x2.5 m passage trigger, the travel axis and placement are unchanged (scripts/world/stormwood_crown_arch_hero.gd). The grass clearance shrinks so moss grows to the pillars. Crystal texels get the blue-vein glow.

round2_candidate._why: P2-041 round 2 (GPU WD2 1 Nov, 4.78: neither side reads as an arch; the square slab is still exposed). On: the hero arch visual turns 90 deg to face the road that reaches the landing (stormwood_arches.json e_crown yaw 90 sets the travel axis across the road, so every road approach and the catalogue view saw the arch edge-on as a single pillar; the near-square 2.2 x 2.5 m passage trigger and colliders are unchanged), stands 7.0 m (from 5.5) so it clears the trainer, and edge_dressing sets half-sunk installed rock-family stones (mossy grey) along the slab's four edges (each edge keeps a 4 m opening at its middle) so the square outline reads as a mossy stone landing. Visual only; footing collider, passage trigger and travel axis unchanged (stormwood_crown_arch_hero.gd with_round2/_dress_slab_edges). OFF until GPU judged.

_why_slab: Hiding the slab mesh would float the trainer 0.2 m on the unchanged footing collider; the slab is re-skinned with the Stormwood wet-moss ground texture instead so it reads as a raised moss bank.
